title: Preserve token-boundary integrity with per-layer asymmetric quant profiles for callable outputs
creator: Asha Raman
description: Background: We observed regressions in callable/JSON-like outputs after applying global FP8/INT8 quantization profiles during a runtime rollout. Existing checks catch schema mismatches but miss subtle tokenization boundary shifts that break consumer RPC parsing. This ticket scopes experiments and an automated validation workflow that focuses on token-boundary preservation across per-layer asymmetric quant profiles and targeted calibration. Goal: identify quant profile configurations and calibration signals that maintain function-call accuracy (call parsing + parameter fidelity) while still delivering >30% throughput/cost gains over baseline float runs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) An automated validation pipeline that computes token-boundary integrity metrics and flags regressions (see metrics below).
2) A set of per-layer asymmetric quant profile candidates with calibrated scales that pass the golden-rpc testbench at target thresholds on our canonical prompt set.
3) Integration of the check into the CI gate: PRs that change quant tables fail CI if callable failure rate increases by >= 1% relative to the float baseline across the canonical trace set.
4) Runbook notes for rollback criteria and a canary rollout policy documented in PR and rollout playbook.
proposed_solution:
1) Implement per-layer asymmetric quant profiles (separate scale/zero points per channel where applicable) instead of global symmetric tables for problematic attention/feedforward layers.
2) Expand the calibration harness to emit 'calibration signature vectors': per-layer scale distribution histograms and boundary-sensitivity scores.
3) Build a token-boundary integrity checker that: a) tokenizes both reference (float) and quant outputs, b) aligns token sequences to detect shifted boundaries, c) computes a boundary-shift rate and JSON-token-edit-distance for callable outputs.
4) Add synthetic golden RPC trace generator to augment real customer traces (obfuscated).
5) Run batch experiments across candidate profiles and collect telemetry. Select top-2 candidates by combined cost/accuracy score and promote through canary funnel.
test_plan:
- Unit: add tests for boundary-aligner algorithm with edge cases (multi-byte tokens, escaped characters).
- Integration: end-to-end runs on our canonical prompt corpus (2k prompts) comparing float baseline, symmetric INT8, symmetric FP8, and per-layer asymmetric INT8/FP8 candidates.
- Statistical: run KS test on token-length residuals and bootstrap confidence intervals on callable-failure rates.
- Load: cherry-pick 1000 golden RPC traces under production-like batching to ensure no latency regressions excluding acceptable quant overhead.
- CI: new gating job that fails on callable failure delta >= 1% or median JSON edit distance > 0.5 tokens over baseline.
metrics: callable_failure_rate_delta: percentage difference vs float baseline
boundary_shift_rate: fraction of outputs with token boundary misalignments
median_json_token_edit_distance: median token-level edit distance on parsed callable fields
throughput_delta: percent throughput improvement vs baseline
p99_latency_delta: p99 latency difference vs baseline
rollout_plan:
1) Lab evaluation (this ticket) -> select 2 profile candidates.
2) Internal canary (10% traffic on dedicated cluster, monitor callable failure rate + error budget) for 48h.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 72h with automated rollback if callable_failure_rate_delta >= 0.5% at a checkpoint.
4) Full promotion behind feature flag with nightly audits for 7 days.
risks: False negatives: token-boundary checker may miss semantic breaks that only appear in rare traces
Calibration overfitting: synthetic prompts might bias scale choices and hurt real traffic
Performance trade-offs: per-layer asymmetry can hurt kernel fusion and reduce throughput gains
Operational complexity: additional calibration artifacts to store and manage per-model-version
